sections.heading: Current distortion near zero crossing
sections.text: Totem-pole PFC current distortion near the AC zero crossing is caused by: (1) dead-time between the fast-path and slow-path switches, (2) inductor current discontinuity in CRM/DCM, (3) insufficient current-loop bandwidth. Increase current-loop crossover or use interleaved modulation.

sections.heading: 120Hz output ripple
sections.text: The PFC output has inherent 2*f_line ripple from the power pulsation. The voltage-loop bandwidth MUST be below 2*f_line (~120Hz for 60Hz, ~100Hz for 50Hz) to avoid current distortion. If the ripple is excessive, increase the output capacitance — do not raise the voltage-loop bandwidth.

sections.heading: Overshoot from voltage loop
sections.text: PFC voltage-loop overshoot: the bandwidth is already very low (<20Hz typical). If overshoot occurs, the kp is too high for the slow plant. Reduce kp and increase ki for steady-state accuracy without overshoot.

sections.heading: ZVS loss at light load
sections.text: Totem-pole PFC with GaN/SiC loses ZVS at light load because the inductor current is discontinuous. This is a topology limitation. Consider: (1) CRM operation with variable frequency, (2) adaptive dead-time, (3) burst mode at light load.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the totem-pole PFC cannot meet THD or efficiency specs, consider: (1) interleaved PFC for lower current ripple, (2) Vienna rectifier for three-phase applications, (3) conventional boost PFC with bridge rectifier if GaN/SiC is not available.
